initial.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / material and surface-paint treatment.
Asset: one existing team logo transformed into a restrained MODERN BLUE-AND-WHITE PORCELAIN edition, titled conceptually "青花出舱", but NO text in the image.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 is the ORIGINAL LOGO and the exact geometry edit target. Preserve its leaning angular H-like body, two diagonal connecting structures, elliptical orbit's existing visible arcs and front/back occlusions, lower-left circular node, and upper-right rocket including its nose, fins and connections. Do not reinterpret or redraw the skeleton.
Image 2 is ONLY a part-separation diagram: its orange parts identify the visible ELLIPTICAL ORBIT, and its gray-blue parts identify the body, diagonal connectors, rocket, and circle. IGNORE ALL colors, background and flat medium in image 2. It is NOT a style reference.

PRIMARY CHANGE:
Turn the gray-blue parts of diagram 2 into warm WHITE PORCELAIN with very sparse refined cobalt underglaze decoration. Turn ONLY the orbit into a confidently painted COBALT BLUE stroke. The final palette is exclusively porcelain white #F7F5F0, cobalt #2F5FA7, a little dark cobalt #1F4175 and extremely pale cool porcelain shading #E9EEF4. No orange, gold, silver or third accent hue.

BODY:
White porcelain is clearly dominant: at least 75–80% of the broad body surface remains unpatterned warm white. Very subtle satin glaze, restrained soft cool edge shading and softly diffused reflections give a warm ceramic feel, not a flat white vector. Keep the facing surface nearly planar, no chunky extrusion, no cast shadow, no visible side thickness. Keep razor-clear geometric silhouette and original sharp corners. A fine quiet cobalt/gray-blue edge inside the silhouette may help white read against light backgrounds.
In just TWO or THREE broad areas, paint short sparse abstract cobalt ridge/water-wave/ascending cloud-breath gestures, following the body's upward-right slant and structural direction. Each group contains only a few deliberate brush marks, varying in taper and pigment concentration under clear glaze, separated by large expanses of bare porcelain. Decoration should cover about 15–20% of the BODY, not a dense all-over repeat. Abstract design strokes only: no literal landscape picture, no complete mountainscape, no traditional clouds with curls repeated everywhere. No flowers, leaves, lotus scrolls, dragons, phoenixes, traditional borders or wave-fill pattern.

ROCKET:
Preserve the exact original compact pointed rocket geometry and upper-right orientation. Mainly porcelain white. Only one or two tiny cobalt strokes on its broad nose, following the direction of flight. Keep fins clean and mostly plain. Do not add portholes, exhaust, panels, metallic seams, new attachments, wings, or decorative bands. Narrow diagonal connecting structures remain white porcelain, not blue orbital strokes.

ORBIT:
Only the original visible left/rear arc and lower/front/right arc become cobalt. Preserve the source geometry and width. Render a controlled continuous underglaze brushstroke with subtly uneven pigment density, deep pooled cobalt in a few portions and softer medium blue elsewhere. Variation follows the arc, not a shiny gradient. Its edge stays clean, no sprawling ink bleed, no broken strokes. Never draw a new complete ellipse over the H or rocket. All source separation gaps remain fully open.

CIRCULAR NODE:
A quiet white porcelain bead with a very fine soft cobalt rim on one side, one soft diffused glaze light and a tiny cobalt dab, largely blank white. Not a planet, marble or glass orb.

COMPOSITION / OUTPUT:
A single logo, exact frontal shape and source aspect ratio, centered on a square 2048x2048 canvas with effective logo width about 75% of canvas. Keep all extremities visible. Output a genuine TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND, clean alpha including every internal negative-space gap; not a white square or a checkerboard pattern. We will place this transparent asset on #FAF8F4 for the presentation.
Modern polished craft design, calm refined blue-white clarity. First read the recognizable logo, only then notice delicate porcelain and brushwork.
NO text, caption, year, seal, calligraphy, NASA, frame, seal border, extra stars, new planets, scene, poster, table, props, fabric, antique paper, photography setting, crackle, wear, dirt, yellow staining, chips, metallic/iridescent shine, glass, plastic, heavy 3D modeling, glowing effects, dense Chinese ornament or ink-wash illustration.

refinement.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input 1 is the blue-and-white porcelain logo EDIT TARGET. Input 2 is the original silhouette reference. Make a SINGLE targeted refinement to the existing porcelain edition, keep its composition and all shapes, source aspect ratio, four identifying parts, delicate internal gaps, and orbit front/back overlaps.

The current decorative waves in image 1 are too literal and busy. REMOVE the crashing-wave / foamy-seascape motifs entirely. Replace them with SPARSE ABSTRACT blue-and-white porcelain craft brushwork, following the H's upward-right leaning structure:
- In the broad upper-left H stroke, only THREE or FOUR short tapered cobalt ridge gestures, slightly uneven pigment, layered diagonally upward-right, with large blank porcelain between them. These are simplified peak-rhythm / water-line marks, NOT a miniature landscape or a breaking ocean wave. No foam.
- In the broad right H stroke, only TWO or THREE shorter, separated gently arcing cobalt water-rhythm strokes on one portion. No dense filled blue patch, no wave crest, no repeated pattern across the whole leg.
- Keep the lower-left broad part almost entirely blank porcelain.
- Patterns occupy roughly 15% of the body and the white porcelain first impression dominates.
- On the rocket nose keep only ONE or TWO tiny thin directional cobalt strokes. Remove the large dark blue patch currently at its tip. All rocket fins and the slim connecting structures stay primarily unpatterned white porcelain.
- Keep the small lower-left bead mostly white, with only a very restrained one-sided cobalt rim/dab.

Also slightly reduce the hard bright edging and strong beveled highlights. The shape has a softly satin-fired porcelain glaze, warm #F7F5F0 with extremely pale #E9EEF4 soft shading, near-planar facing surface. NO glossy metal trim, no silver rim, no thick 3D extrusion or plastic shine. Retain enough delicate cool inner-edge definition for the white silhouette to read.

Preserve the existing complete COBALT ORBIT, original thickness and occlusions; its natural blue pigment concentration variation is good. Keep it continuous, hand-painted underglaze cobalt #2F5FA7 with occasional #1F4175 depth, not an ink wash splatter. Avoid cyan or electric saturated blue.
No new objects, text, seals, captions, frames, stars, planets, clouds, oldness, cracks, chips, gold, or orange.
Output one logo on genuine TRANSPARENT background, all holes transparent, same framing as input 1. High-quality original modern porcelain craft logo, sparse precise decoration, not a poster or product photograph.
